problem_type: Deletion leaves an empty storyboard group frame
symptom: Deleting the last shot node in a storyboard group leaves an empty group frame; deleteNode, deleteSelectedNodes, and cutSelectedNodes can diverge.
direct_cause: Each deletion path removed node ids from a group or removed fully covered groups independently, without one shared post-delete group lifecycle rule.
class_root: The shared node deletion boundary did not enforce that a non-empty group made empty by the current deletion is removed in the same state transition, while preserving user-created empty groups.
affected_population: All canvas users deleting one or more nodes through sidebar, canvas, agent, keyboard, menu, storyboard undo, or cut entry points
Existing grouped nodes and persisted user-created empty groups
internal_only_reason: This is an application-owned canvas state invariant; no third-party behavior determines group lifecycle.
invariants: A group with members before the deletion is removed iff all of its members are in the current deleted node set.
A group with remaining members keeps exactly those remaining node ids.
A user-created group that was already empty is preserved.
Deletion and its group cleanup share one undo snapshot.

door_reduction.why_not: These UI, sidebar, agent, storyboard, and derivation doors remain distinct callers, but all converge on the three store actions; the shared helper enforces the invariant without changing their entry semantics.

generality_proof: The helper is called by deleteNode, deleteSelectedNodes, and cutSelectedNodes before each state write. Door-map coverage shows every checked caller reaches one of those actions, so the same group lifecycle rule applies across UI, agent, sidebar, storyboard, and derived-node deletion.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Filter deleted members from every group, remove only groups that were non-empty and become empty, and preserve pre-existing empty groups.
Apply the shared group cleanup with the node and edge deletion in one undo snapshot.
Apply the same shared group cleanup for cut operations in one undo snapshot.

invariant_owner_layer.why: All three deletion actions converge on the shared group transition before their state writes.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Direct node deletion calls removeGroupsEmptiedByNodeDeletion before its state write.
Selected deletion uses the same helper and emits group removal events in the same gesture.
Cut deletion uses the imported helper before its single undo snapshot and event batch.

recurrence.reason: Three distinct store deletion actions and 19 caller/read doors can reproduce the same empty-group state unless the invariant is centralized.

prevention.invariant: Only groups that had members before this deletion and have no remaining members afterward are removed; all other groups retain filtered membership.
prevention.failure_mode: The state write uses the helper result atomically with the node and edge deletion; there is no caller-specific fallback cleanup.
prevention.strategy: Make every deletion action call the same pure group transition before writing state and emitting one gesture.

legacy_paths.rationale: The obsolete behavior was inline state logic, not a standalone legacy path; it was replaced in place by the shared boundary.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No third-party dependency controls this state invariant.

migration: No persisted data migration is needed. Existing user-created empty groups remain; only groups made empty by a new deletion are removed.
residual_risks: The parallel canvas-explicit-delete line may alter event/history plumbing; merge integration must preserve this helper at the shared deletion boundary.
